title: Twists at the Pretzel Bakery
description: Explore pretzel shapes and bakery vocabulary through loops, coarse salt, and a tray of dough.
cardDescription: Explore pretzel shapes and bakery vocabulary through loops, coarse salt, and a tray of dough.
focus: A pretzel’s knotlike outline gives several clues their setting. The terms distinguish shaping actions from the dough, surface, and finished baked item.
solvingTip: Use a shape or action first, then cross the words for ingredients and baking equipment.
words: PRETZEL
Twisted baked bread often finished with coarse salt
TWIST
To turn a strip of dough around itself
LOOP
Curved enclosed opening in a classic pretzel shape
COARSE
Describing large salt crystals on a pretzel's surface
GLAZE
Thin surface coating giving a baked item a sheen
DOUGH
Unbaked flour mixture shaped into a pretzel
SALT
Crystalline seasoning visible on many pretzels
YEAST
Microorganism helping many soft pretzel doughs rise
TRAY
Flat support holding shaped pretzels in an oven
KNOT
Interlaced form suggested by the pretzel's outline
OVEN
Heated enclosure in which pretzels bake
CRUST
Browned outer layer of a baked pretzel
FLOUR
Ground grain powder forming much of the dough
ROLL
To shape dough into a long thin rope

answerNotes.PRETZEL: Pretzels can be soft or crisp; the familiar twisted shape does not require only one texture.
answerNotes.TWIST: Twisting describes the shaping action, while the dough remains the material being shaped.
answerNotes.LOOP: A loop is a shape feature rather than an ingredient or a baking stage.
answerNotes.COARSE: Coarse concerns crystal size; it is different from how salty the entire bread tastes.
answerNotes.GLAZE: Glaze names a coating or finish; its ingredients depend on the item being made.

title: A Bagel Before Breakfast
description: Identify a bagel through its ring shape, chewy texture, and the words for preparing and serving it.
cardDescription: Identify a bagel through its ring shape, chewy texture, and the words for preparing and serving it.
focus: A familiar bagel is boiled before baking. The clues separate that preparation step from a serving choice such as toasting or adding a spread.
solvingTip: Look for the stage described: shaping, cooking, or serving.
words: BAGEL
Chewy breakfast ring commonly topped with sesame or poppy seeds
CHEWY
Offering some resistance to the bite, as a bagel often does
SESAME
Small pale seed commonly used as a bagel topping
POPPY
Plant name completing ___ seeds, a familiar bagel topping
SPREAD
Soft topping applied across the cut face of a bagel
RING
Circular shape with a central opening
HOLE
Open space through the middle of a bagel
DOUGH
Unbaked mixture formed into a bagel
BOIL
To cook in bubbling hot water before the baking stage
BAKE
To cook using the dry heat of an oven
TOAST
To brown a cut bagel surface before serving
KNIFE
Cutting utensil used to divide a bagel
FLOUR
Main ground-grain ingredient in bagel dough
YEAST
Raising organism used in many bagel doughs

answerNotes.BAGEL: Boiling before baking helps distinguish a traditional bagel from an ordinary ring-shaped roll.
answerNotes.CHEWY: Chewy describes texture rather than flavor or temperature.
answerNotes.SESAME: Sesame is a topping ingredient, distinct from the flour in the dough.
answerNotes.POPPY: The clue concerns the small food seeds used on baked goods, not a flower's petals.
answerNotes.SPREAD: Spread can be a noun for the topping or a verb for applying it.

title: A Waffle Iron on the Counter
description: Explore a familiar breakfast through its patterned cooking plates, batter, and toppings.
cardDescription: Explore a familiar breakfast through its patterned cooking plates, batter, and toppings.
subtheme: A Waffle Iron on the Counter
focus: A waffle takes its patterned shape from heated plates. The clues distinguish the appliance from the mixture poured into it and the food served afterward.
solvingTip: Use the difference between tool, uncooked mixture, and topping to guide the crossings.
words: WAFFLE
Breakfast cake cooked between patterned heated plates
GRID
Regular crossing pattern impressed into a waffle
BATTER
Pourable uncooked mixture placed in a waffle iron
HINGE
Joint allowing the waffle iron's top to open and close
SYRUP
Sweet pourable topping served over many waffles
IRON
Traditional name for the patterned waffle-cooking appliance
PLATE
Heated patterned surface inside a waffle maker
POCKET
Small recessed square in a cooked waffle
CRISP
Firm and lightly brittle, as a waffle's browned exterior can be
BUTTER
Dairy spread melting into a warm waffle
FORK
Pronged utensil used to eat a waffle
MILK
Liquid ingredient in many waffle batters
EGG
Ingredient contributing structure to many breakfast batters
STEAM
Water vapor released as a waffle cooks

answerNotes.WAFFLE: A waffle's characteristic grid comes from the cooking plates rather than being cut into it afterward.
answerNotes.GRID: Grid describes the surface pattern; the pockets are individual recesses within it.
answerNotes.BATTER: Batter is the mixture before cooking, not the cooked waffle or the appliance.
answerNotes.HINGE: A hinge connects movable parts while permitting rotation.
answerNotes.SYRUP: Syrup is a topping, while sugar may also be part of the uncooked batter.

title: A Sourdough Starter Jar
description: Explore a fermenting bread culture through its flour, bubbles, and familiar vocabulary of growth and acidity.
cardDescription: Explore a fermenting bread culture through its flour, bubbles, and familiar vocabulary of growth and acidity.
focus: A sourdough starter is a culture containing yeasts and bacteria. Its bubbles and changing aroma reflect fermentation rather than the action of baking powder.
solvingTip: Separate the living culture from the vessel, ingredient, or visible sign of activity.
words: STARTER
Maintained culture of flour, water, and microbes used for sourdough
CULTURE
Community of microorganisms grown in a prepared medium
YEAST
Fungus contributing gas production in a bread starter
FERMENT
To undergo microbial activity that changes a mixture
LACTIC
Describing an acid associated with bacteria in sourdough
FLOUR
Ground grain mixed with water to maintain a starter
WATER
Liquid combined with flour in the culture
BUBBLE
Small gas pocket visible in an active mixture
JAR
Container holding a maintained sourdough culture
RISE
To increase in volume as gas collects in a mixture
AROMA
Smell noticed when opening the starter container
TANG
Pleasantly sharp flavor associated with sour bread
DOUGH
Bread mixture to which a mature culture may be added
FEED
To add fresh flour and water to maintain the culture

answerNotes.STARTER: A sourdough starter commonly contains both yeasts and lactic acid bacteria.
answerNotes.CULTURE: Culture has a biological meaning here, distinct from the arts or social traditions.
answerNotes.YEAST: Yeasts help produce carbon dioxide during fermentation; bacteria also contribute important changes in sourdough.
answerNotes.FERMENT: Fermentation describes biological change, not simply flour becoming wet.
answerNotes.LACTIC: Lactic acid is one contributor to sourdough's acidity; several products affect its overall flavor and aroma.

title: Noodle Dough on the Board
description: Follow the shapes and tools of handmade noodles through rolling, cutting, and a board dusted with flour.
cardDescription: Follow the shapes and tools of handmade noodles through rolling, cutting, and a board dusted with flour.
focus: Noodles can be made from many grain ingredients and recipes. This scene focuses on rolled dough and the distinctions between sheets, strands, and serving texture.
solvingTip: Use the resulting shape: a broad sheet, a thin strand, or a small cut piece.
words: NOODLE
Strip or strand of dough cooked as food
SEMOLINA
Coarse milled durum-wheat product used in many pastas
ROLLINGPIN
Cylindrical dough-flattening tool, with spaces omitted
STRAND
Long thin piece of noodle dough
ALDENTE
Italian phrase for firm to the bite, with spaces omitted
FLOUR
Powder dusted over a noodle-making board
DOUGH
Uncooked mixture rolled into a noodle sheet
EGG
Ingredient included in many homemade noodle mixtures
SHEET
Broad thin layer of rolled noodle dough
CUT
To divide the rolled dough into strips
BOARD
Flat work surface beneath the dough
FORK
Utensil used to gather cooked noodle strands
DRY
To remove moisture from freshly shaped noodles
SAUCE
Flavorful accompaniment served with cooked noodles

answerNotes.NOODLE: Noodle is a broad food word; ingredients and shapes differ among traditions.
answerNotes.SEMOLINA: Semolina names a wheat product, not a ready-made pasta shape.
answerNotes.ROLLINGPIN: Rolling pin is continuous in the grid; the tool flattens the dough rather than cooking it.
answerNotes.STRAND: A strand is a shape description; a sheet is broader and has not yet been divided into narrow pieces.
answerNotes.ALDENTE: Al dente describes a cooked texture rather than a particular noodle shape.
